message.content: {"rules":["Allocator implementations permit zero-sized allocations; if an underlying allocator does not support them or returns a null pointer for them, the implementation must handle that case.","A memory block is currently allocated by an allocator if its starting address was previously returned by that allocator's allocate, grow, or shrink method and it has not subsequently been deallocated. Calling deallocate or a grow or shrink operation that returns Ok deallocates the old block; a grow or shrink operation that returns Err does not.","Where a method requires a layout to fit a memory block, the block must be currently allocated with alignment equal to layout.align(), and layout.size() must be within the inclusive range from the size of the layout used to allocate the block to the actual block size returned by allocate, grow, or shrink.","Currently allocated memory blocks must point to valid memory and remain valid until the block is deallocated or the allocator is dropped.","Copying, cloning, or moving an allocator must not invalidate memory blocks returned from it.","A copied or cloned allocator must behave like the original allocator.","A currently allocated memory block may be passed to any method of its allocator that accepts such an argument."]}
